extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, their counsel, and USPTO disciplinary stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and procedural requirements for an affidavit of resignation (exclusion on consent) submitted to the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline, and the resulting obligations, publications, and presumptions affecting reinstatement. Focused on practitioner disciplinary/resignation process before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation must be freely and voluntarily rendered
rubrics_metrics.description: His consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiant must explicitly acknowledge that the decision to submit the affidavit is voluntary and not the result of coercion or duress. This is a required element for approval under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must acknowledge awareness of OED investigation and specific allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: He is aware that the OED Director opened an investigation of allegations that he violated the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, namely: OED File No. G2239. The investigation concerned allegations, inter alia, that: (a) By Final Order dated April 12, 2013, Respondent was suspended for five years ... for neglecting patent matters by allowing patents to expire for not timely paying maintenance fees, for failing to inform clients of important USPTO correspondence and giving misleading information to clients about the status of their patents. He also failed to conduct an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances prior to signing and filing certain submissions with the USPTO; (b) By Final Order dated April 12, 2013, Respondent was granted limited recognition ...; (c) Respondent engaged in the unauthorized practice of law in the prosecution of U.S. Trademark application nos. 85/906,074 and 85/906,085 by representing clients before the USPTO while he was not authorized to do so; and (d) Respondent did not inform his clients or the trademark examiner ... that he was not authorized to represent the clients before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit should identify that an investigation exists and describe the nature of the allegations (examples: neglect of patent matters such as failing to pay maintenance fees; failing to inform clients of correspondence; giving misleading status information; failing to make reasonable inquiry before filings; unauthorized practice of law in trademark matters). Including specific factual allegations supports the affidavit's validity under 11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must acknowledge the specific rules alleged to be violated
rubrics_metrics.description: He is aware that the disciplinary complaint pending against him alleges that he violated the following provisions of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct: (a) 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(a); (b) 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c); (c) 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d); and (d) 37 C.F.R. § 11.505.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit should state awareness of the particular regulatory provisions alleged to be violated. Listing the exact regulatory citations (e.g., 11.804(a),(c),(d); 11.505) is part of the required acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment re: reinstatement presumption of allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Without admitting to any of the allegations ... Respondent acknowledges that, if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (a) the allegations set forth ... are true and (b) he could not have successfully defended himself against such allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiant must accept that for future reinstatement proceedings under § 11.60 the Office will treat the pending allegations as conclusively true and that the affiant could not have successfully defended against them. This is a legal consequence of consenting to exclusion and is material to approval of the affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiant must demonstrate understanding of relevant USPTO regulations and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60, and is fully aware of the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit should state that the respondent has read and understands the cited regulations (including their practical consequences). This confirms informed consent and is necessary for approval under § 11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiant must expressly consent to exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: He consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear statement of consent to exclusion from practice (patent, trademark, other non-patent matters) is required. The Office will only accept an affidavit seeking exclusion on consent when the respondent affirmatively agrees to exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director approval under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 required for exclusion on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation shall be approved and Respondent shall be excluded on consent from practice before the Office ... For the reasons set forth herein, Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation shall be approved and Respondent shall be excluded on consent ... Based on the foregoing, the USPTO Director has determined that Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director must determine the affidavit meets the regulatory requirements of § 11.27(a) before approving exclusion on consent. The final order language evidences the standard of review and formal approval step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 upon exclusion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires the excluded practitioner to follow the duties spelled out in § 11.58 (e.g., obligations that arise upon suspension/resignation/exclusion such as client notification, file transfer, handling of pending matters—affidavit should reflect awareness and intent to comply).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 following acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office must take the actions required by § 11.59 after accepting an affidavit of resignation/exclusion on consent (e.g., publication, notification duties). The Final Order directs OED to follow those regulatory duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any reinstatement request
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the excluded practitioner later seeks reinstatement, the practitioner must satisfy the procedural and substantive requirements of § 11.60. The affidavit should acknowledge this future obligation and the consequences (including the reinstatement presumption noted above).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish this Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's electronic FOIA Reading Room ... The OED Director shall publish the following notice in the Official Gazette: Notice of Exclusion on Consent ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of an affidavit of resignation triggers publication duties: posting in the OED Reading Room and publishing a notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion, allegations, and implicated rules. The Final Order specifies text and where to publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior misconduct examples constituting neglect of patent matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglecting patent matters by allowing patents to expire for not timely paying maintenance fees, for failing to inform clients of important USPTO correspondence and giving misleading information to clients about the status of their patents. He also failed to conduct an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances prior to signing and filing certain submissions with the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order lists concrete examples of practitioner misconduct (failure to pay maintenance fees, failure to inform clients, misleading clients, inadequate inquiry before filings) that support suspension/exclusion; these act as anti-patterns practitioners must avoid and are the types of conduct investigated under USPTO disciplinary rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice of law in trademark matters and related failures to disclose
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent engaged in the unauthorized practice of law in the prosecution of U.S. Trademark application nos. 85/906,074 and 85/906,085 by representing clients before the USPTO while he was not authorized to do so; Respondent did not inform his clients or the trademark examiner ... that he was not authorized to represent the clients before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order treats representing clients while not authorized and failing to disclose lack of authorization to clients/examiners as disciplinary misconduct (proscribed by 37 C.F.R. § 11.505). Practitioners must ensure they are authorized before representing clients and must disclose authorization status where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable ethical framework depends on date of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility applies to practitioner misconduct that occurred prior to May 3, 2013, while the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq., apply to practitioner misconduct that occurred after May 2, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of which ethical/regulatory standards govern alleged conduct depends on the date the conduct occurred. Affidavits and disciplinary actions should reference the correct ethical code based on timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of disciplinary proceeding upon carrying out agreement terms
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO Disciplinary Proceeding No. D2014-22 is hereby dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an affidavit of resignation/exclusion on consent is approved and the parties carry out the terms (including exclusions and regulatory obligations), the underlying disciplinary proceeding may be dismissed as part of the order.
